comments.author: @chiwayway2010
comments.text: I lived here for 4-1/2 years when my husband was working on a project there. Many artesian wells were put into villages and the cities by foreign embassies, so the people had good, clean, water. We boiled all our water. There's no malaria as the stagnant water is too polluted for the larvae to grow, or mosquitoes to breed. We never got seriously ill, at least not from water borne diseases. We enjoyed our time there. There are many NGOs operating there, trying to help. Governments send millions to them yearly for various needs. The markets breed a lot of germs because of the way the people use the markets for defecation etc. That's why it was very important to clean all vegetables well, before cooking. We never ate salads. I visited a factory outside of Dhaka. It was clean, well run, and the workers were fed meals when on shifts. We were given a very nice meal served on large leaves and eaten with our right hands. (The left hand is considered "dirty" as it is used for personal ablutions.) Yes, there are sweat shops but you show me any city where unscrupulous bosses try not .to get the most out of their workers, especially from those who are illegally in a country. Yes, there is child labour, and severe poverty, but when you see the alternative work for children ( ie prostitution) factory work is a better alternative. It's governments that have to change their people. The west cannot interfere in certain cultural laws and traditions. It is up to the individual government to help lift their own people out of poverty, and help with health issues and whatever other help their people need.  Foreign aid is already abundant.
